definitions.quantiles: floor(n*q), matching the original harness; all selected samples contribute. No trimming, winsorization, host-load filtering, or failure deletion.
definitions.timing: measure.started+sample[0] is the sample timestamp after play.frame and before subsequent observer work, not a C++ or rAF exit. Actual rAF wrapper and JS onGameFrame entries/exits are retained separately. Original rawSummary names/definitions are preserved verbatim.
definitions.phases: pre-active ends at the first wrapper with a recorded active sample; startup-active ends at the first wrapper reaching frame 180. Formal-active runs until measure.ended; limit-tail samples are separately marked. Every >100ms completed entry, dispatch, wrapper, sample and submission gap is retained, including startup. All final pending requests are retained with right-censored snapshot ages.
definitions.ordinary: oneForwardNoReplay requires adjacent sample frontier +1 and unchanged correction/resim counters; it never includes no-forward callbacks. The strict subset additionally requires capture +1, Present +1, and non-wait return. Both preserve every selected raw index; this is a counter-based classification, not native phase instrumentation.
definitions.rawAvailability: Original report SHA and exact paths retain the full event arrays. Compact output retains full host rows and audio blocks, all threshold breaches and unmatched records, all pacing network-brake episodes, and explicit selected maxima.

environmentSourceObservation.scope: Read-only observation of the current Playwright dependency, not a browser trace or retrospective file snapshot. Under the current noDefaults=false main-frame flow, document.hasFocus may be emulated. The recorded true values cannot prove foreground, non-overlap, or physical visibility; these defaults alone do not identify the rAF cause.

cpuThrottle.scope: openProbe and after-open counters precede CPU throttling; subsequent netplay setup and first game callback use the configured per-side rates.

raw.scope: Read-only host CPU counters and candidate process CPU counters. No performance samples are excluded or reweighted.
limitations: Aggregate CPU occupancy does not establish single-core availability, CPU frequency, thermal state, GPU load, or a stable benchmark environment.
Process names are candidates for contention, not proof that a process is compiling. Known harness/relay/helper PIDs are labeled separately; other node processes remain unlabeled candidates.
Process CPU is cumulative lifetime CPU seconds. A first sighting is not CPU consumed during this run; PID reuse or counter reset can break a delta.
The 5 s process snapshots miss short tasks that start and exit between snapshots. Timer delays and source/receive times are retained.
This observer has overhead. Its own PowerShell helper is intentionally not a candidate process, but its work is included in aggregate CPU counters.
